title: [HW2] Route every debate message through the controller (child -> father -> child) (P1)
prompt: Decide with the grader's intent in mind — either (a) document that the orchestrator+controller jointly satisfy the mediation, or (b) refactor so each message is explicitly routed through the controller (father) before reaching the opponent. If (b): keep context isolation + anti-sycophancy intact; TDD; <=150 lines/file; ruff/mypy/coverage >=85%.
note: HW2 docs/hw2_requirements.pdf §8.3.7 — the debate must flow THROUGH the father: every message goes child -> father -> child; debaters never communicate directly. Chose option (b): made the CONTROLLER the explicit relay hub. Added packages/core/src/agent_debate/core/engine/forward.py: forward_to_opponent(message, from_side, to_side, round_, run_id, runs_dir, sink) — the father's forward step. It frames the message via the existing build_adversarial_relay (reused, NOT duplicated: sanitised + '«…». Rebut it.') and logs one structured 'system' routing event tagged message_routed_through_controller carrying from/to sides + round (agent='controller') — the demonstrable evidence the message passed through the father. Refactored engine/loop.py: after each debater turn + drift-check, the loop calls _forward(...) -> forward_to_opponent to route the produced message through the controller, then the opponent's next _turn rebuts the controller-FORWARDED frame (not the raw turn). engine/turn.py: run_debate_turn's opponent_message param renamed framed_opponent_message (already-framed, controller-forwarded text), folded into the same anchor user turn via anchor_turn — the turn helper no longer re-frames. A FAILED turn forwards nothing (None) so the opponent gets a fresh anchor (§4 graceful degradation). New constants LOOP_RELAY_EVENT_TYPE/LOOP_RELAY_LOG_AGENT/LOOP_RELAY_EVENT_TAG (no schema break; reuses 'system' event type). Isolation (5.4) + adversarial framing (5.6) + side-anchoring + drift-check/nudge + 10-vs-10 + word-limit + timeout/retry + verdict all preserved unchanged; relay_opponent_turn kept as a still-exported building block. TDD red-first: packages/core/tests/test_controller_relay.py drives the real engine loop offline and asserts (1) forward_to_opponent invoked per message before reaching the opponent (spy + logged routing event, alternating pro->con/con->pro), (2) opponent still receives the §5.6 frame, (3) Con only ever sees Pro's content wrapped in the frame (isolation), (4) drift-check still nudges a conceding Pro. Updated existing tests whose call path legitimately changed: test_system_prompt_delivery.py, test_engine_acceptance.py, test_acceptance_criteria.py — renamed opponent_message= -> framed_opponent_message= on direct run_debate_turn calls. Gates green: ruff check + format clean, mypy clean (254 source files), check_line_limit.py exit 0, pytest --cov 99% total (forward.py 100%). No NEW failures vs clean main: 6 pre-existing environmental failures unchanged (2 Unix file-permission branch-protection checks, 2 live-tree secret-scan/hygiene on the developer's real .env, 2 Windows missing-file path-regex) plus the 2 long-topic parametrized teardown errors. secret_scan.py flags only the developer's real local .env (pre-existing). docs/PRD.md NOT touched (PR #214 owns it).
